Having preheat leading the weld, or on the sides of the weld could control the defect formation such as cracking, or slow down cooling time of the weld pool to enable the escape of trapped gas and thus limit porosity. However, there would need to be more research to determine if the added complexity of the system provides sufficient benefit. The liquid in the weld pool is shaped by several factors including the surface tension which holds the liquid in the joint, gravity, fluid flow, and the pressure from the keyhole vapor column. Orienting the beam in the horizontal direction in mitigates the effect of gravity which can make an underbead that conforms to the required geometry. Another advantage of horizontal EBW is the ability to stack components on a turn-table motion system(C-axis rotation) [50, 51]. When the design permits, this significantly simplifies the need fixturing as horizontal EBW utilizes gravity to locate and hold parts. Horizontal EBW is beneficial when welding large, heavy components such as turbines assemblies, rocket nozzle bells and nuclear pressure vessels because of the favorable loading conditions on the rotary motion system.
